structured.answer: The 2026-10-01 files look filtered, not truncated. Orders has no `web` rows at all, and web is normally about half of daily orders. The files cover the whole day, are complete and well-formed, and have no gaps in the order_id sequence. I found no manifest or metadata, and the logs have no mention of web.

findings.claim: Orders landing for 10-01 has 235 rows against 461 on 09-30. Header matches the contract, there are no parse problems, and the file ends with a newline. It looks structurally complete.

The `web` channel is entirely absent on 10-01: 2 distinct channels against 3 on 09-29 and 09-30. app (151) and marketplace (84) are at normal levels, in line with their 09-11 to 09-30 ranges. web ran 203–283 per day and drops to 0. This is a missing segment, not a time-of-day cutoff.

Order timestamps span 00:23 to 23:55 on 10-01, so the file is not cut off by time of day. Order IDs run 13404–13841 with 235 distinct IDs, continuing from 13401 on 09-30. The 10-01 range spans 438 IDs but only 235 are present, so the roughly 200 missing IDs are probably the web orders. The first IDs, 13402 and 13403, are also absent (the 09-30 file ends at 13401).

order_items (464 rows) and payments (219 rows) are also well-formed and end on complete lines at orders 13841 and 13840. Both fall in the same order_id range as the filtered orders file, so they look downstream of the same web-less order set. Payments methods are all present (card 127, gift_card 50, paypal 44) at roughly half the 09-30 counts (251, 91, 96). That uniform halving means no method is missing, which fits the loss of one channel's orders.

The landing inspection shows no manifest or completeness metadata, and `ingest_config` is empty for these tables, so ingest is not dropping web. A log search for 'web' returned nothing. I did not check the status distribution, and I did not compare order_items with order_id. The cause is upstream, most likely a source-side export filter or failure for web. Confirm with the upstream owner.

args.query: row_count_trend row count drop partial export

evidence.text:
## Verification
- Rerun the partition. `partition_present`, `row_count_trend` and `reconciliation` must pass.
- Row counts for the day are now within the normal range of prior days.
- Hour and channel distributions match prior days.
- `assert_order_totals_match_items` and `assert_payments_match_orders` pass.

## Symptoms
- dbt tests fail: `unique_stg_orders_order_id`, `unique_stg_order_items_order_item_id`, `unique_stg_payments_payment_id` or similar, with N failing rows.
- `reconciliation:raw.orders->marts.fct_orders` fails: mart row count exceeds distinct raw orders.
- Revenue for a day is inflated; `row_count_trend` may fail on the high side (above 160%).
- Staging models do no dedup, so duplicates in raw flow straight to marts.

## Symptoms
- `ingest` fails: `landing file missing: landing/<table>/dt=<date>/<table>.csv` (loud).
- Check `partition_present:raw.<table>` fails: `raw.<table> partition <date> has 0 rows` (silent: an empty file loads fine).
- Check `row_count_trend:raw.<table>` fails: today's rows fall outside 60%-160% of the trailing 7-partition median.
- Check `reconciliation:raw.orders->marts.fct_orders` fails: distinct raw orders for the day differ from `fct_orders` rows.
- Check `freshness:marts.fct_orders` fails: latest order date in the mart is behind the partition.
- Business symptom: revenue or order count for a day looks too low.

## Step 1: Which tables are affected?
- Compare row counts by `_dt` for `orders`, `order_items`, `payments` against the previous 7 days.
- Orders, items and payments are related. A drop in one with others normal suggests a partial export of that table.
- If all three dropped by a similar proportion, the export for the day was truncated or filtered across tables.

args.query: filtered export low-volume day redelivery escalation upstream

evidence.text:
## Escalation
- Model logic or intentional change: `analytics_engineering`.
- Export or file problem persisting after redelivery: `upstream_app_team`.
- Infrastructure or orchestration: `data_platform`.

## Remedy for one-off export glitches
- Use `request_upstream_redelivery` for the day with ALL affected related tables together: `orders`, `order_items`, and `payments` (add `customers` only if it is also affected).
- Redelivery re-runs the export and produces a correct file for each table.
- Redelivering just `orders` when items/payments were also cut leaves referential mismatches.
- Then rerun the partition and verify.

## Why asking upstream to resend does NOT fix this
- Renames, new columns, drops and reformatting are deliberate, persistent upstream changes applied to every export from an effective day onward.
- A redelivery re-runs the export and reproduces the same changed file, with the same header and formats.
- `request_upstream_redelivery` is for one-off export glitches only (missing, truncated, duplicated files).
- If the change is wrong from upstream's point of view, that is a conversation with `upstream_app_team`, not a resend.

## Choosing quickly
| Finding | Action |
|---|---|
| landing file missing / row drop (partial or filtered) | `request_upstream_redelivery` (orders, order_items, payments) |
| corrupt or truncated file | `request_upstream_redelivery` |
| duplicates within one file | `deduplicate_on_ingest` or redelivery |
| stale rows from a previous day | `request_upstream_redelivery` |
| renamed column | `apply_column_mapping` |
| `$`-formatted amounts | `set_column_parser` (`strip_currency`) |
| new non-contract column | `ignore_extra_columns` |
| required column dropped, no source | `escalate_to_owner` (`upstream_app_team`) |
| changed dbt model broke build or numbers | `revert_model_change` |
| transient, cause cleared | `rerun_only` |
| nothing safe applies | `escalate_to_owner` |

structured.answer: The runbooks treat a simultaneous drop in orders, order_items and payments as a truncated or filtered export. The recommended fix is to ask upstream to redeliver all the affected tables together, then rerun the partition and verify. Escalate to upstream_app_team only if the problem persists after redelivery. I didn't find a runbook section that explicitly separates a filtered export from a genuine low-volume day. The only hint is the hour and channel distribution check in Verification.

findings.claim: row_count_trend:raw.<table> fails when the day's rows fall outside 60%-160% of the trailing 7-partition median. A low-side failure is a missing, partial or filtered-data symptom. A high-side failure (above 160%) points to duplicates instead.

Partial vs filtered: compare orders, order_items and payments by _dt against the previous 7 days. A drop in one table with the others normal suggests a partial export of that table. A similar proportional drop in all three means the export was truncated or filtered across tables.

Genuine low-volume day: the runbooks I retrieved have no explicit criteria for this. Verification expects row counts back in the normal range and hour and channel distributions matching prior days. That implies hour and channel skew (for example, missing hours or a missing channel) would indicate a filtered or truncated export. This is my inference, not stated text.

Remediation is redelivery. Use request_upstream_redelivery for the day with all affected related tables together (orders, order_items, payments, and customers only if it is also affected). Redelivering orders alone leaves referential mismatches. Then rerun the partition and verify that partition_present, row_count_trend and reconciliation pass, and that assert_order_totals_match_items and assert_payments_match_orders pass.

Escalation goes to upstream_app_team, but only for an export or file problem that persists after redelivery. Model-logic problems go to analytics_engineering. Infrastructure or orchestration problems go to data_platform. Escalate_to_owner is also the fallback when nothing safe applies.

Redelivery only fixes one-off glitches (missing, truncated or duplicated files). It does not fix deliberate, persistent upstream changes such as schema changes, which are a conversation with upstream_app_team. If the drop recurs across days, or the redelivered file looks the same, the problem is probably not a one-off glitch. That reading is my inference.

structured.summary: The `nightly` run f6a6201b for 2026-10-01 failed in quality_checks. raw.orders, raw.order_items and raw.payments are each at about 50% of their trailing median, because upstream's export for that day left out every `web` order. The files are otherwise complete and cover the full day. No dbt models changed and the ingest config is the default, so the pipeline isn't the cause. I've proposed asking upstream to re-export all three tables for 2026-10-01, then rerunning.

root_cause.explanation: Upstream's 2026-10-01 export has no `web` orders, and web is normally about half of daily volume. app and marketplace counts are normal, timestamps cover the whole day and the files are well-formed, so the export was filtered by channel rather than cut off. order_items and payments only cover the orders that were exported, so they dropped by the same proportion. Ingest and dbt passed the rows through as delivered: ingest config is default and no models changed.

evidence.claim: quality_checks failed only on row_count_trend for raw.orders, order_items and payments, each at about 50% of the trailing median. The other 34 checks passed.
The low counts were already in the landing files: ingest loaded 235, 464 and 219 rows.
The `web` channel is entirely missing on 10-01, while app and marketplace are normal and timestamps cover the full day.
The pipeline isn't the cause: no dbt models changed and the ingest config is the default.
The runbook says a proportional drop across related tables means a truncated or filtered export, and the fix is to redeliver all of them together.

alternatives_considered: Partial or truncated export: ruled out because timestamps run 00:23–23:55, the files end cleanly, and the drop is limited to one channel.
Bad model deploy: ruled out because no dbt models changed.
Genuinely low-volume day: unlikely, because app and marketplace are normal and only web fell to zero.
Web channel deliberately shut down upstream: not ruled out. If the redelivered files still have no web orders, escalate to upstream_app_team.
rerun_only: wouldn't help, because the landing files themselves are missing the web orders.
